title: bug: moe-daemon start (and _run) on a --project with no .moe/ logs "Another process is starting the daemon, waiting..." then "Failed to acquire lock and daemon not running" and exits 0, because acquireLock folds ENOENT into lock contention and the lock-failure branch returns without an exit code
description:
Filed by the 11-03 #6 defect hunt (task-cea8fa39, architect-1dd28c7c). Found by a hunt subagent; I re-ran the repro myself.

PROBLEM
- packages/moe-daemon/src/index.ts:274-283, acquireLock: the catch is `if (err.code === 'EEXIST') {...} return false;`. Every other error returns the same `false` as a held lock: ENOENT when .moe/ is missing (the O_EXCL create of .moe/daemon.lock fails), and also EACCES and ENOTDIR.
- index.ts:695-708, startDaemon: on `false` it logs "Another process is starting the daemon, waiting...", waits LOCK_RETRY_DELAY_MS (2000 ms by default, :48), logs "Failed to acquire lock and daemon not running" at error level, and `return`s. `_run` exits 0.
- index.ts:1036-1040, superviseDaemon's exit handler: code 0 means "Daemon exited cleanly" and `process.exit(0)`. So `start` exits 0 too.
So a typo'd or never-initialized --project looks like a successful start, and the log blames a race that never happened. The genuine case ("lock held, and the other starter never brought a daemon up") exits 0 as well.

Precedent in the same file: existingDaemonBlocksStart (:646-668), the shared first gate of start/init and _run, already reports a refused start with `process.exitCode = 1` and returns true (the foreign daemon.json case). The CLI promises exit codes elsewhere: doctor "exits 1 on any hard fail", check-architecture 0/1/2.

EVIDENCE (HEAD 19d5e67a, git-archive snapshot, env scrubbed with `env -i PATH=... HOME=<scratch> NODE_ENV=production`)
1. Mine: in /tmp/hunt-cea8-snap/packages/moe-daemon, `node --import tsx src/index.ts _run --project <empty dir> --port 19471` logs
   {"level":"info",...,"msg":"Another process is starting the daemon, waiting..."}
   {"level":"error",...,"msg":"Failed to acquire lock and daemon not running"}
   and then rc=0. The project dir stays empty.
2. Subagent, /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-cea8/A/start-no-moe-exit0-repro.txt: `node dist/index.js start --project /tmp/hunt-cea8-A/proj-nomoe --port 19451` logs "Supervisor spawned daemon process", "Another process is starting the daemon, waiting...", "Failed to acquire lock and daemon not running" and "Daemon exited cleanly", then rc=0. A path that does not exist at all (.../proj-nomoe/typo) gives the same rc=0.
3. A failing vitest: /mnt/d/moe-scratch/hunt-cea8/A/index.start-no-moe.repro.test.ts (output in start-no-moe-vitest.txt). It spawns `_run` on a dir without .moe/, and both soft assertions fail: the output contains "Another process is starting the daemon", and the status is 0.

FIX DIRECTION
- Refuse a project with no .moe/ before any lock or spawn. Extend the shared first gate (or add a sibling check that start, init and _run all pass) with a clear error such as ".moe/ missing at <path>; run moe-daemon init --project <path>" and `process.exitCode = 1`. `start` then never enters the supervisor's crash-restart loop. `init` creates .moe/ first, so it is unaffected.
- Make acquireLock stop presenting non-EEXIST errors as contention. Return a reason, or rethrow, so the "Another process is starting" message appears only for EEXIST.
- When the daemon is still not running after the lock wait, exit non-zero.
Keep the existing acquireLock and stale-lock behaviour and tests unchanged.

FILES
- packages/moe-daemon/src/index.ts
- packages/moe-daemon/src/index.test.ts (test)
Out of scope: src/tools/** (hunt #5's lane) and doctor.ts.

NOTE FOR THE PLANNER
The spawn tests must scrub the seat's MOE_* env and use a scratch HOME. `_run` writes ~/.moe/config.json after a successful start. Set MOE_LOCK_RETRY_DELAY_MS small to keep the lock-wait case fast.
definitionOfDone: A test in packages/moe-daemon/src/index.test.ts spawns `node --import tsx src/index.ts _run --project <tmp dir without .moe> --port <free>` with a scrubbed env and a scratch HOME. The exit status is non-zero, the output names the missing .moe/, and the output does not contain "Another process is starting the daemon".
A second spawn test runs `start` on the same kind of dir. It exits non-zero within 10 s, with no "Restarting daemon after backoff" line: a missing .moe/ is final, not a crash.
`cd packages/moe-daemon && npx vitest run src/index.test.ts` passes, with the existing acquireLock and stale-lock cases unchanged.

implementationPlan.description: Fix in packages/moe-daemon/src/index.ts with the Edit tool. Reference: /mnt/d/moe-scratch/plan-88673297/fix.diff (sha256 e00e03522d2eb6c4..., 90 lines). Its base ce5ff130 is byte-identical to the current moe/work-2026-10-24 tip for this file. (a) acquireLock (:253): in its catch keep the EEXIST branch byte-for-byte, and change the trailing `return false;` to `throw err;`, so ENOENT/EACCES/ENOTDIR are never reported as contention. Add a doc comment: false means a held non-stale lock, or our own failed write (cleaned up); any other create error throws. (b) Add the module-private `function missingMoeDirBlocksStart(projectPath: string): boolean` right before existingDaemonBlocksStart's doc comment (:646). Inside try/catch: `fs.statSync(path.join(projectPath, '.moe')).isDirectory()`. Any stat error, or a .moe that is not a directory, refuses. On refusal: `logger.error({ projectPath, moeDir }, `.moe/ missing at ${projectPath}; run moe-daemon init --project ${projectPath}`)`, then `process.exitCode = 1`, then return true. Otherwise return false. It creates nothing. (c) startDaemon: (1) call `if (missingMoeDirBlocksStart(projectPath)) return;` before `if (await existingDaemonBlocksStart(projectPath)) return;` (:692). (2) Wrap acquireLock in try/catch: `logger.error({ error, lockPath: lockFilePath(projectPath) }, 'Could not create the daemon lock'); process.exitCode = 1; return;`. (3) In the lock-wait failure branch, add `process.exitCode = 1;` after 'Failed to acquire lock and daemon not running' (:706). (d) superviseDaemon (:992): make the same gate its first line, before existingDaemonBlocksStart, so `start` exits 1 without spawning `_run`. `init` never trips the gate, because initProject creates .moe/ first (:1302-1304). The supervisor gate is what keeps DoD 2's no-restart: the supervisor's exit handler treats every non-zero child exit as a crash. Error handling: every refusal logs exactly one error line that names the path, sets process.exitCode = 1 and returns. This follows the existingDaemonBlocksStart precedent (:646-668), and it never calls process.exit(), so pino flushes. acquireLock's write-failure cleanup (unlink, 'Failed to write daemon lock; removed it', return false) and its EEXIST/stale-lock handling stay unchanged. No new export. Do not touch src/tools/** or doctor.ts (out of scope).
implementationPlan.note: Added missingMoeDirBlocksStart (gate in startDaemon + superviseDaemon before existingDaemonBlocksStart); acquireLock throws non-EEXIST errors; startDaemon catches lock errors and sets exitCode 1 on the lock-wait failure.

implementationPlan.description: Adversarial self-review of this task's diff (adversarial-self-review skill), then run checkRef 3. It checks scope: exactly packages/moe-daemon/src/index.test.ts and packages/moe-daemon/src/index.ts changed against the merge base, and no forbidden pattern added. Checklist: (1) the '.moe/ missing' gate runs before existingDaemonBlocksStart in both startDaemon and superviseDaemon, and creates nothing (N1, N2). (2) 'Another process is starting the daemon' is logged only after a non-stale EEXIST (N1, N4). (3) Error handling: every refusal sets exitCode 1 and returns, with no process.exit(). (4) A .moe that is a regular file or a dangling symlink refuses at the gate. A .moe/ the daemon cannot write (EACCES) passes the gate and refuses at acquireLock ('Could not create the daemon lock', exit 1). (5) A genuine lock race: the losing `start`'s _run now exits 1, so its supervisor runs its bounded crash-restart (1 s, 2 s, 4 s..., at most 5 in 60 s). It exits 0 once the winner answers 'Moe daemon already running', else 1 'Too many restarts'. That is intended (the task's FIX DIRECTION), not a regression. (6) A .moe/ removed after the supervisor started is caught by _run's own gate: exit 1, bounded restarts. That is acceptable; add no supervisor recheck. (7) Tests: the scrubbed env leaks no MOE_* variable; scratch dirs are removed in afterEach; freePort avoids port collisions; nothing relies on the 2000 ms default wait. Kill only PIDs your own session started, never by pattern (project rail).

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: Return a reason enum from acquireLock instead of throwing: rejected. It churns every call site, and index.test.ts (:186-223, :401, :558, :646) and atomicWrite.test.ts:285 assert its boolean. Throwing keeps the boolean contract for EEXIST and makes every other create error loud. Folding the .moe/ check into existingDaemonBlocksStart: rejected. That function's contract is daemon.json; a sibling gate called first in both entry points keeps each readable. Creating .moe/ on start: rejected. init owns scaffolding, and a typo'd --project must not grow a .moe/ (N2).
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: superviseDaemon's exit handler treats every non-zero child exit as a crash and restarts with backoff (1 s, 2 s, 4 s..., at most 5 in 60 s). Only code 0 means 'Daemon exited cleanly' (:1036-1040). So a final refusal must happen in the supervisor itself before spawn, not only in _run. Under NODE_ENV=production, pino logs one JSON object per line, which the tests parse for msg. LOCK_RETRY_DELAY_MS reads MOE_LOCK_RETRY_DELAY_MS at module load (:48). The 'native aliases of --project' tests already resolve tsx with createRequire (:473). Launchers and IDE plugins spawn `start` in the background and poll daemon.json, never trusting its exit code (MoeDaemonSupervisor.kt:696, MoeDaemonClient.ts:721, moe-agent.ps1:1029). Docker runs `start --project /project` with restart: unless-stopped, which restarts on any exit code.
planningNotes.risks: N3 at the base needs NODE_OPTIONS=--import <tsx>, or its child fails on the .ts import (the wrong failure). spawnSync blocks the vitest worker for up to 30 s per row; rows normally take 0.3-1 s. On Windows, HOME and USERPROFILE both point at the scratch home, and SystemRoot/TEMP/TMP are passed through. Do not edit existing rows. Write tracked files only with Edit/Write. A lost genuine lock race now goes through the bounded supervisor restart instead of exiting 0 at once (see step 4, item 5).
